----------

**Welcome back!** Hundreds of Claude conversations turned up in Google results with wallet keys and personal details inside, the model that hacked Hugging Face left notes teaching future versions how to break out, Anthropic shipped a beast at half of Fable's price and Fable 5.1 is already lined up for August.



**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** What did the rogue model leave behind?

* **Opus 5:** When should you use it over Fable?

* **Fable 5.1:** What's landing next month?






----------

----------
## [Your Claude chats showed up on Google](https://tech.yahoo.com/ai/claude/articles/people-found-crypto-wallet-data-185133771.html)

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/8f98d834-2ce8-4c38-9669-1bdbf8c64215/Beehiiv_01_-_Jul_25.png?t=1785143805)
Caption: 

Someone searched Google over the weekend and found hundreds of people's Claude conversations sitting there in plain view.

They were chats users had shared with a link, and those pages were missing the tag that tells Google to stay out. So the whole conversation got crawled and indexed.

The contents are the problem. People found crypto wallet data, API keys, resumes with home addresses and phone numbers, internal company projects and social security numbers.

A share link was only ever meant for the person you sent it to. Post it once in a forum or a group chat and Google can find it forever.

Anthropic appears to have pulled the pages from Google since, though users report some still surfacing on Bing.

If you have ever hit share on a Claude chat, go check what is in it.

76536.subject: 💰 The Funding: Are crypto vaults funds and curators fund managers?
76536.body:
The SEC's Hester Peirce says some of them may be — which could mean registration. Here's what that means, and what comes next.

The Funding ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Yogita Khatri | Edited by Zack Abrams

Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 56th edition of The Funding!

*SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce* recently signaled ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409409/you-will-have-a-painful-fall-secs-peirce-warns-crypto-vault-builders-against-twisting-securities-law?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) that some crypto vaults may fall under federal securities laws. What does that mean for the fast-growing vault space, and who across it is most at risk? I reached out to vault protocols, curators, investors, and legal experts to find out what Peirce's statement means and what comes next. Let's dive in.

*THE INSIDE VIEW*

*Are crypto vaults funds and curators fund managers?*

Earlier this week, SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce published a statement ( https://www.theblock.co/post/409409/you-will-have-a-painful-fall-secs-peirce-warns-crypto-vault-builders-against-twisting-securities-law?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) saying crypto vaults and onchain lending strategies may already fall within federal securities laws. Moving an activity onchain does not, as a general matter, take it outside those laws, she wrote. Anyone doing "headstands, backflips, and other gymnastics to read the law so that it does not apply" to activities within its scope "will have a painful fall."

Peirce set out several ways the laws could apply ( https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/peirce-statement-crypto-vaults-lending-strategies-072226?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ). A vault could be a common enterprise in which users invest money expecting profits from the efforts of its deployer and curator. A vault that holds securities, or allocates assets to securities, could fall under investment company laws. Depending on how it operates, a vault could resemble a unit investment trust, a management investment company, or a separately managed account (which all require different levels of SEC registration). Onchain loans could also be notes that are securities, while managing vaults or lending strategies may raise investment adviser issues.

Whether any of these laws apply "will come down to the specific facts and circumstances," Peirce wrote. She invited firms to come and talk. The statement is not a rule or an enforcement action, and Peirce spoke only for herself, not the Commission. But it marked the second time in three months that SEC leadership had publicly addressed vaults.

In May, SEC Chair Paul Atkins said ( https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/atkins-remarks-scsp-ai-expo-050826?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknew
